answer: A refundable stake tied to verified work makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a marble-sized deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it cheated. A lone sparrow cannot multiply into a flock for free, because every copy pays the same stake. Reputation then accrues only at the jetty where real services are delivered, so an attacker must fund each identity and risk losing every stake, while honest agents earn theirs back with interest.
